Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Benjamin Waterhouse (author, Wikidata Q2896275), died 1846. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Waterhouse, Benjamin, 1754-1846") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: A journal of a young man of Massachusetts [microform] : late a surgeon on board an American privateer, who was captured at sea by the British, in May, eighteen hundred and thirteen, and was confined first at Melville Island, Halifax, then at Chatham, in England, and last, at Dartmoor prison : interspersed with observations, anecdotes and remarks tending to illustrate the moral and political characters of three nations : to which is added a correct engraving of Dartmoor prison, representing the massacre of American prisoners, Boston : Printed by Rowe and Hooper, 1816, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cihm_41868. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 49%, 85%, 93% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Benjamin Waterhouse, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
